interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 50.20 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 37.65–62.75 months; its coverage has not been validated.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2c, negative surgical margins, no seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis. These favorable pathological findings are positive prognostic factors. The preoperative PSA was 11. The surgical findings, including negative margins and no nodal metastasis, support a favorable outcome.

Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA level and the missing biopsy grade and ISUP report, which introduce uncertainty regarding the true tumor characteristics. Missing nodal sampling information, although the record indicates sampling occurred, widens the uncertainty regarding complete nodal status assessment. The postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical for revising this prognosis. Further postoperative PSA measurements are necessary to assess the current disease control.

attempts.text:
The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2c. Favorable surgical findings included negative surgical margins, no seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis. The preoperative PSA was 11. The surgical pathology report documented, "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5), pathological stage pT2c. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis."

These positive surgical findings are favorable prognostic factors. However, the preoperative PSA of 11 is a significant factor. The absence of documented recurrence suggests a long-term outlook, with the expert horizon suggesting a heuristic sensitivity range for recurrence extending up to 62.75 months. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up information widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial to refine the prognosis.
